articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA, the agency that's supposed to protect everyone else's infrastructure, just got caught with their own pants down after a contractor leaked AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub. Congress is rightfully losing their shit over this spectacular own-goal.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: A CISA contractor casually dumped highly privileged AWS GovCloud credentials and internal agency secrets on public GitHub because apparently irony is the only thing government cybersecurity does well. Peak operational security right here, folks.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: AI is apparently getting really good at finding vulns in human code, which explains why this month's Patch Tuesday looks like a CVE explosion. The robots are coming for our bugs before they come for our jobs.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: EFF analysis reveals cops are using license plate readers for everything from school enrollment checks to noise complaints because mission creep is the most predictable feature of surveillance tech. Warrant? What warrant?

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare win for end-to-end encryption, reminding us that keeping our digital conversations away from prying eyes is still possible when done right. Small victories in the eternal crypto wars.

articles.title: Company CEO flooded file share with smut, called for help after he deleted it
articles.summary: ShinyHunters ransacked Carnival Cruise Lines for 6 million customer records because apparently their security was as watertight as the Titanic. Just another day in the ShinyHunters world tour of corporate incompetence.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Claude Security Plugin, Azure Priv-Esc, Kali365 MFA Bypass, FIFA Scams +15 More
articles.summary: Microsoft throws a tantrum about public zero-day disclosures after GitHub researcher accounts get nuked, demanding everyone play nice with coordinated disclosure. Classic Microsoft: shoot the messenger, blame the community.

articles.title: Cogent Security launches autonomous vulnerability response tools as AI-assisted exploits outpace scanners
articles.summary: Cogent launches AI-powered tools to close the exploit-to-remediation gap because traditional scanners move like molasses while exploits spread at light speed. Finally, someone building defenses that match the pace of modern attacks.

articles.title: Tucker Carlson Doles Out Some Truly Strange Credit Card Advice
articles.summary: Indian student hacker claims to have breached CBSE's exam evaluation system while the board insists it was just a 'testing platform' - because nothing says educational integrity like arguing over which system got owned. Plot twist: the kid disputes their damage control.

articles.title: Cogent zeroes in on zero-day response for rapid remediation
articles.summary: CBSE's digital exam portal faces government audit after scoring glitches and hack claims surface, proving that even standardized testing isn't immune to the universal law of digital clusterfucks. IIT gets called in to clean up the mess.
